newsitem.title: UK: East Midlands Electricity up on Dominion offer.
newsitem.headline: East Midlands Electricity up on Dominion offer.

text.p: Shares in East Midlands Electricity were indicated sharply higher on Wednesday after Dominion Resources announced an agreed 670p cash offer for the regional electricity company.
The shares were indicated 16-1/2p higher at 627-1/2p by 0817 GMT in pre-market trade.
The bid values East Midlands Electricity at about 1.3 billion stg. U.S. company Dominion said last week that it was considering an offer "at a price not much in excess of 608p per share."
"It seems a sensible price," said one head of equity sales. "But it comes as no real surprise as it was a fairly public courtship."
East Midlands chairman Sir Nigel Rudd said the board was recommending the cash offer because it represented fair value.
But traders said gains in the share price were likely to remain capped amid regulatory worries.
"Everyone's expecting the MMC (Monopolies and Mergers Commission) to take a close look at the deal," said one trader. "That is why the shares are only trading around 630p."
